Nicole Buchanan for NPR hide caption toggle caption i Nicole Buchanan for NPR American women today are having fewer children than their mothers and grandmothers did. They also have more opportunities and life choices. "I don't really feel like I got strong messages about what my life should look like beyond college graduation," said Caroline Brown, 33, of Charlotte, N.C.. "I was very much under the impression that the world was kind of my oyster." Like a growing number of younger women, she's unsure if she wants children. And she's not unusual; the U.S. birthrate now is about half of what it was in the 1960s. Caroline's grandmother, Barbara Briscoe, 93, says during her childbearing years, there wasn't a big question about what she was going to do with her life. pages.text: 30-30 club broken down by team Skip to Content The marvel of the 30-30 club is predicated on the rare combination of speed and power it takes to swipe 30 bases and bash 30 homers in the same season. A record seven players joined the club in 2025: Juan Soto , Jazz Chisholm Jr. , José Ramírez , Corbin Carroll , Francisco Lindor , Pete Crow-Armstrong and Julio Rodríguez . PCA became the first player to join the club in 2026, making it two straight seasons for the Cubs superstar, and Washington's CJ Abrams and Cincinnati's Elly De La Cruz joined the party later in the year. The feat has been pulled off 82 times in AL/NL history. Here is a team-by-team breakdown of the 30-30 club, ranked in order from the team with the most 30-30 seasons to the least -- there are actually six teams that have never had someone pull off the feat. (Note: We list franchises together, even if the club moved.) pages.text: 33 Chilean Miners Were Buried Alive. These Are the Tactics That Kept Them Sane. | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE 33 Chilean Miners Were Buried Alive. These Are the Tactics That Kept Them Sane. As the world raced to rescue the trapped miners in a disaster that made international headlines, two psychologists were tasked with maintaining everyone's mental health. Chilean Minister of Mines Laurence Golborne holds a note from the miners while President Sebastián Piñera gives a speech during rescue operations. Miguel Soffia By Angela Posada-Swafford Published September 25, 2026 For Alex Vega, the morning of August 5, 2010 started off just like any other. He headed towards the San José mine in Chile’s Atacama region, then descended 2,100 feet into the ground to start his work. Suddenly, after four hours on the job, he and the other men working alongside him heard several high-pitched, whistling noises. Then came deeper, thunder-like sounds, followed by the rumbling noise of fast-flowing rocks. The mine had collapsed. The 33 miners were practically buried alive in an environment boasting 95°F heat, 98 percent humidity, and absolute darkness. “The initial thundering and the bangs we kept hearing meant enduring another psychological weight at the thought of the mountain sinking before rescuers reached us,” recalls Vega. The incident gained global media attention, with dozens of news organizations gathering outside the mine alongside the miners’ family, friends, and other onlookers—all of whom were looking to the Chilean government for answers. However, 2D-projected anisotropy images cannot provide out-of-plane angles of molecules. Over the last ten years, the NIST Biomaterials group has developed a novel theory and experimental methods for measuring 3D orientation angles using 2D polarization imaging acquired with transmission IR and coherent Raman microscopy. This rapid, non-invasive imaging technique helps understand the molecular-level structure of highly anisotropic and spatially heterogeneous materials. Hanacek/NIST It seems like many items in our everyday lives have been getting more expensive lately. Here at NIST, we are committed to making sure you get what you pay for when buying something based on weight or measure, such as food or fuel. We also work to make sure sellers get fair payment for the goods and services they provide. Today marks the first day of Weights and Measures Week , when we celebrate the anniversary of President John Adams signing the first U.S. weights and measures legislation into law.
